name: How do I know if my bathroom has hidden water damage?

mainEntity.name: What are the signs that a bathroom remodel will uncover hidden water damage behind tile or under the floor?
mainEntity.text: What are the signs that a bathroom remodel will uncover hidden water damage behind tile or under the floor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden water damage is one of the biggest variables in bathroom renovation cost and schedule. Warning signs include soft spots in the floor, cracked grout that keeps returning, loose or hollow tile, swelling at the base of walls, rusted fixtures, mold odors, and staining on ceilings below the bathroom. In older homes, even a bathroom that looks fine can have damaged subflooring or framing behind the walls. That is why contractors often cannot give a truly firm price until demolition begins. Homeowners should ask whether the estimate includes a damage allowance, how change orders are handled, and what happens if rotten framing or a failed shower pan is discovered. The safest assumption is that any old bathroom may need some level of concealed repair once opened up.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common signs of hidden water damage include soft flooring, loose tile, stained drywall, mold smell, peeling paint, and a shower that has leaked into adjacent walls or ceilings. Once the walls or floor are opened, contractors may find rotted subfloor, damaged studs, or failed waterproofing.
